- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from 14d avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent high.
- If sentiment turns negative mid-horizon, model fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per 3-day negative sentiment window.
- Model underestimates mean-reversion zones (e.g., below 65–67) when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias if sentiment > 0.05.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often lags 1–2 days behind true trend; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment is trending upward.
- If sentiment is volatile (±0.3 or more), reduce forecast volatility by 20–30% to avoid overfitting to noise.
- When sentiment is negative and price is above 70, model tends to overcorrect; apply downward pressure of 0.5–1.0% per 3-day negative sentiment streak.
